messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High 5xx rate detected from inference-prod in us-west-2a (alert_id=INC-2468). p95 latency increased from ~320ms -> ~12s, 5xx rate 18% -> 65% across model-serving nodes in az1a. Suspected ENI/NAT egress saturation. https://alerts.redwood/INC-2468

SRE Oncall (Mike C): taking it. moving discussion here. Anyone seeing console anomalies?

Adele (Support): multiple support tickets from customers reporting timeouts and 502s on text-generation endpoint. Examples: convoai-prod, docqa-ingest. Customers report timeouts ~10-15s then 502. Escalated to priority.

Neha P: I see host network errors on several g5-type hosts in us-west-2a: RX errors spiking, tx queue drops, and kernel logs showing 'dev eth0: transmit queue stop'. NAT gateway metrics show active connection count >> baseline and high drop_count. Likely egress bottleneck.

SRE Oncall (Mike C): ok immediate plan: 1) shift traffic away from us-west-2a (smart routing) 2) scale capacity in other AZs (2b/2c) where we have spare GPUs 3) enable temporary model-fallback to lower-memory/quantized variants for new requests to reduce egress and memory pressure. 4) inform customers & status page.

Neha P: executing traffic shift now. Using ops traffic tool to steer away from az1a. Command:
```
./traffic-ctl shift --from az=us-west-2a --to us-west-2b,us-west-2c --percent 70 --dry-run=false
```

Deploy Bot: traffic-ctl change applied (change-id: shift-2468-01). Route policy updated; partial steering enabled. DNS TTL for endpoint is 30s — steering applies at LB/proxy layer for sticky connections.

Runtime - Lee: enabling model-fallback rule for route inference-prod: prefer quantized-small for new sessions to cut downstream bandwidth. Patch applied:
```
route_config(inference-prod):
  fallback_priority: [quantized-small, quantized-medium, float-small]
  new_session_only: true
```
Result: ~40% of traffic now landing on quantized-small variants (based on routing weights).

Infra Bot: provisioning additional GPU nodes in us-west-2b/2c. Autoscaler started +40 instances; expected ready ~8-10m.

Adele (Support): status.redwood message drafted and posted: "Partial degradation in us-west-2a affecting text generation. Traffic being routed to other AZs; mitigation in progress. Some requests may see increased latency or 502s. We will provide updates every 15 minutes." Link: https://status.redwood/incident/INC-2468

Product - John: tagging Dedicated customers and account execs. Any SLA exposure? We should notify accounts ops.

SRE Oncall (Mike C): I'm going to call handoff at 15:05UTC. Neha, can you take lead for the mitigation and postmortem? I'll stay on the bridge for 10 more minutes to confirm handoff.

Neha P: I can lead. Opening a PM channel and creating timeline doc. First triage notes in the doc: observed NIC tx/rx_queue stalls on 6 hosts, NAT gateway active_conn spike to 4x baseline, multiple long-lived client connections causing NAT exhaustion.

SRE Oncall (Mike C): small additional mitigations: 1) disable long-lived sticky session routing from problematic customers when possible (reduce sticky cookie TTL), 2) enable prefix-level caching for common prompts to avoid repeated token generation. Applying caching TTL bump to 30s for identified prompt sets.

Runtime - Lee: applied prefix/KV cache tweak for the top 20 prompt fingerprints. Should reduce token regen for retried requests.

Support Bot: customers with open tickets updated via support portal and email. On-call support rota alerted.

Neha P: monitoring metrics now — after shift and scaling: 5xx rate from traffic hitting us-west-2a clients dropped from 65% -> 12% in 5m. Overall platform p95 improved from 12s -> 1.2s for routed traffic. We still see sticky session tails causing a small error tail for sessions pinned to az1a (~5% of traffic).

Incident Bot: incident state updated to 'mitigating' (INC-2468). Conference bridge created: https://meet.redwood/INC-2468-1

SRE Oncall (Mike C): handing primary duty to Neha at 15:12UTC. I'm switching to watcher. Escalation path: if errors spike >20% again, failover to full cross-region (us-west -> us-east) + customer notification.

Neha P: accepted handoff. Next actions: continue steering until ENI/NAT errors clear, drain affected hosts for host-level recovery (kubectl cordon/drain pattern), and coordinate with cloud provider if ENI limits are being hit. Starting drains on 6 hosts now:
```
for host in host1 host2 host3 host4 host5 host6; do
  kubectl cordon $host && kubectl drain $host --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
done
```

Infra Bot: drain jobs scheduled. Observed kernel logs show 'ENI detach throttled' on one host — raising to cloud support.

Adele (Support): updating critical customers directly: convoai and docqa have been notified of mitigation and expected recovery window ~30-45m.

Neha P: current status (T+22m): traffic shift in place, scaled nodes online, drains in progress. 5xx global average down to 4.8%. p95 ~1.1s on non-sticky routes. Still monitoring sticky session tails and NAT error counts.

SRE Oncall (Mike C): thanks team. If we keep trending down, we'll move to 'monitoring' in 45m and start RCA. Neha, please capture timeline and initial blameless notes.

Neha P: will do. Posting short timeline and next-steps in the PM doc. Final update in 15m unless regressions. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: incident note appended to customer-facing timeline.

Runtime - Lee: leaving a quick ops note for postmortem: consider per-customer connection limits and NAT gateway sizing for high concurrency workloads; evaluate sticky-session fallback to proxy-level reroute earlier.

Neha P: confirmed at T+48m: residual 5xx ~1.2%, p95 ~0.98s, drains completed, cloud support engaged for ENI/NAT investigation. Transitioning incident state to 'monitoring' in 10m, preparing incident report skeleton.

SRE Oncall (Mike C): acknowledged. Handoff complete. Thanks everyone."
